bulletin.night: Conditions are favourable for further withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon from some more parts of Rajasthan and some parts of Punjab and Saurashtra & Kutch during next 3 4 days.

met_analysis:
Conditions are favourable for further withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon from some more parts of Rajasthan and some parts of Punjab and Saurashtra & Kutch during next 3-4 days. Under the influence of the upper air cyclonic circulation over north Andaman Sea & neighbourhood, a Low Pressure area has formed over the same region at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 19th September, 2026. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify gradually into a depression over eastcentral Bay of Bengal on 21st and into a deep depression over westcentral Bay of Bengal on 22nd September. Continuing to move west- northwestwards it is very likely to reach westcentral and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal near south Odisha- north Andhra Pradesh coasts around 23rd September morning.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over West Madhya Pradesh & adjoining East Rajasthan extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from northeast Uttar Pradesh to Northeast Arabian sea across cyclonic circulation over West Madhya Pradesh & adjoining East Rajasthan and Gujrat State between 3.1 & 5.8 km mean seal level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level with a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 78°E to the north of Lat. 28°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Tripura & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The East-West trough from cyclonic circulation over north Andaman Sea & neighbourhood to North Coastal Andhra Pradesh across central Bay of Bengal extending upto 5.8 km above mean seal level persists.
The North-South trough from north Coastal Andhra Pradesh to Gulf of Mannar across Tamil Nadu at 0.9 km above mean seal level has become less marked.
